messages:
Emma: flagging a customer-reported issue with the .NET SDK paginator + client-side throttle. They see bursty downstream traffic and quota hits despite setting maxConcurrency=4.

Ryan: which SDK version and sample code?

Emma: net sdk 2.0.1, sample usage:

```
await foreach (var page in client.ListUsersAsyncPages(new ListOptions { PageSize = 100 })) {
  Process(page.Items);
}
```

They set ClientOptions.MaxConcurrency = 4 and ThrottleOptions.Enabled=true. Still, server logs show spikes of 50 rps.

Arjun: do they use prefetch or internal buffering? .NET iterator could be pulling next pages synchronously while consumer is slow.

Emma: yes, default prefetch is 5 in net sdk. The client also has an internal channel buffer of size 10. So even with maxConcurrency 4, prefetch+buffer can cause bursts when consumer catches up.

Maya: is throttle implemented per-request or per-transport? If throttling only throttles the send but not the prefetch enqueuer, we can still have bursts queued in memory and released later.

Emma: current throttle token is checked at send time only. Prefetching pulls pages ahead and writes them to internal channel without applying backpressure properly. When channel is full it starts dropping tokens and then flushes quickly, causing bursts.

Ryan: interesting. logs?

Emma: excerpt from customer trace:

```
[21:10:01] prefetch started page=1
[21:10:01] prefetch started page=2
[21:10:02] channel buffered=10
[21:10:05] consumer processed 2 pages
[21:10:05] channel drained -> flush burst 20 requests in 200ms
[21:10:05] server responded 429 x 12
```

Arjun: root causes we see so far:
- prefetch + buffer allows many pages to be queued and then sent quickly (burst)
- throttle only applied at send, not at prefetch/enqueue time, so backpressure signal is missing
- SDK parity: node and py have stricter backpressure (they await enqueue when buffer full) while net uses non-blocking write which drops backpressure

Maya: short term mitigations for customers: set prefetch=0 and reduce internal buffer to 1. Also recommend adding a small processing delay between pages: `await Task.Delay(50)` as a stopgap.

Ryan: midterm fix suggestions:
1) change enqueue to honor the same concurrency semaphore (block when buffer full) so prefetch waits for available permits
2) expose `prefetch` and `internalBufferSize` in public options and make defaults conservative (prefetch=1, buffer=2) to match other SDKs
3) implement jittered release when draining channel to avoid flush spikes
4) add unit/integration tests simulating slow consumer + bursty producer and assert no >maxConcurrency over window

Emma: agreed. I'll file an issue and attach the trace and a small repro. Can we also add a diagnostic metric `sdk.prefetch.queue_depth` and an alert when average > 75% for 1m?

Arjun: yes, telemetry will help. Also let's check other transports: grpc vs http may behave differently; ensure parity.

Maya: docs: quickstart should call out 'prefetch interacts with throttling' and show recommended settings for long-running paginated jobs (example: `prefetch=1, maxConcurrency=4`).

Ryan: who will own the patch?

Emma: I'll pick it up. Plan: repro test in CI, change enqueue to await semaphore, expose options, bump default prefetch to 1, add telemetry, ship 2.0.2 patch.

devex-bot: Created issue #1533: ".NET paginator prefetch + buffer causing quota bursts despite throttling". CI job: https://ci.redwood.ai/job/1533-net-prefetch-repro

Arjun: also add a cross-SDK parity test matrix so we don't diverge again.

Emma: will add tests and update the pagination README. Will notify the customer once a RC is ready. Thanks all :thumbsup:
